No turn-2 sheets: the turn-1 reads already used the call budget. Not verified: the ActiveNet checkout and group-class prices (not shown on any captured page), whether map pins or location names can be clicked, the content of the video tile in the testimonial carousel, whether the balls wobble or the wave text moves by itself or with the scroll (stills only), the text past the 6000-character cut on method and private, and anything on mobile past the 14-screen cap on classes and coaches.

ref-0009.business: Summer Smash Tennis sells public tennis lessons in Vancouver: indoor/outdoor group classes for kids (ages 2-18 in named levels) and adults (NTRP-style 1.0-3.0 levels, plus fitness classes), private lessons (1-6 students), and school programs (only in the nav, not captured). Classes run through community centres and the City of Vancouver Park Board (classes and about pages). The actions that pay: REGISTER on a class card on /classes (27 cards, each with spots left; price shown only as 'Prorated at Checkout', so the checkout is probably at the city/community-centre system: inference), and 'Buy on ActiveNet' on /private (24 buttons, $100 down to $28.50 per person per lesson), then a booking form with a receipt upload. Buyers: parents of children, more than adult learners (four of the seven home testimonials are from parents). Secondary capture: newsletter and 'notify me when registration opens'. Inference: revenue is shared with or collected by the city, which explains why the site cannot show one price and one checkout.

reasons.business: Strong: the first screen splits the two paying routes (GROUP LESSONS / PRIVATE LESSONS, both in the header and the hero, and they stay visible: ref-0009/digest.md Actions, desktop-fold.png). /classes shows real stock per class ('1 spot left', '4 spots left'), a waitlist form for full or unopened terms, and filters by age, level, day and location. /private shows a full price grid with volume and group discounts ('BEST VALUE'). Weak: the home page has no price and no 'from $X' anchor ('Prices: none'). Group-class prices are not shown anywhere captured. The private flow is a 4-step chain across two systems (pay on ActiveNet, save the receipt, come back, upload the receipt again for every single lesson, see a $0 checkout: ref-0009-private/digest.md FAQ), which leaks buyers. The trust before the ask is mostly an unsourced superlative ('VANCOUVER'S BEST') and 'over 10,000 students' in the hero. Real trust assets (city partnership, 40+ named coaches, First Nations programmes, 'since 2012') sit on subpages or near the bottom of the home page.
reasons.customer: The phone visitor (often a parent) asks, in order: is there a class for my child's age/level near me, when, how much, is it good, how do I sign up. The home page answers 'what' and 'for whom' at once (mobile-fold.png: H1, kids-and-adults line, two full-width CTAs). The fall banner answers 'is it on now' with Kids/Adult links. Levels (33%) and locations with a map (51%) follow. It never answers 'when' or 'how much'; you must go to /classes, which does answer when and how many spots, but not price. Testimonials come at 57-70%, one at a time behind arrow buttons; 12 of their texts were never visible during a scroll and stay hidden with reduced motion (inspector FAIL hidden-content and reduced-motion). On a phone, /classes is 12444px tall with 31 tap targets under 24px (ref-0009-classes/digest.md). The banner's Kids/Adult links are 36x23 and 44x23 on every page. The home location list (8) does not match the /classes filter (10, adding Hillcrest, Thunderbird and North Delta, and North Delta is outside Vancouver).
reasons.story: One message holds across the site: a structured way to learn tennis in public facilities ('Progression' + 'Pathway'), repeated by the wavy text band 'THE PATHWAY IS THE PROGRESSION' (sheet-desktop.png page-03) and the /method page with 10 numbered steps. Order on the home page: promise, what is on now (fall indoor classes), levels, method, where, proof, origin, social, newsletter. Each section hands over to the next with one CTA, which works. But the headlines are in the company's voice and stay abstract ('GIVES STUDENTS THE FOUNDATION TO EXCEL AS PLAYERS FOR LIFE'). The customer's voice exists only in the testimonials, which are specific and strong ('ratio of tennis coach to student is perfect', 'playing in less than 4 lessons', 'had to convince them to go each week... night and day') but sit hidden in a carousel below the map. The superlative H1 is never backed up on the page. The ending ('PLAY BEAUTIFULLY' plus a pile of balls) is brand voice, not a last ask.

claims.claim: 1. Tennis balls that wobble; pictures cut through their frame and seem to come out of it
claims.verdict: confirmed with correction (frame break); wobble unverifiable
claims.evidence: desktop-fold.png: the racquets and balls cross the photo borders (left racquet extends right past the frame, right racquet hangs below it). The correct term is 'frame-break' or 'out-of-bounds cutout' layering, not the picture itself leaving its frame: the photo stays cropped and only the drawn props cross the edge. Motion: 7 elements move with no input at the top of the page (digest Motion), which fits idle ball motion, but stills cannot show a wobble. Role note: decorative, does not affect conversion.

claims.claim: 3. Animated text running along a circular / wavy shape is unique
claims.verdict: contested on 'unique'; the device is confirmed
claims.evidence: sheet-desktop.png page-03, motion-sheet.png 07-scroll-2250px: text on a wavy path ('THE PATHWAY IS THE PROGRESSION . THE PROGRESSION IS THE PATHWAY'), plus a round badge 'SUMMER SMASH TENNIS EST 2012' (desktop-page-06). The correct term is 'text-on-path marquee' and a 'circular text badge'. Both are common patterns in playful brand sites, so 'unique' is wrong. What earns its place is the copy: the band repeats the method message right before the method section, so it does story work. The digest counts '0 endless loops with text', so the wave probably moves with the scroll and does not loop by itself (inference; not verified).

claims.claim: 4. The map uses custom objects (tennis-ball pins) and is fun
claims.evidence: sheet-desktop.png page-04, motion-sheet.png 08-scroll-3150px, sheet-mobile.png page-05: a flat, illustrated blue map of Vancouver with tennis-ball markers. The correct term is 'custom map markers on a stylised (likely static SVG) map', not 'objects'. For the visitor, the pins carry no labels in the stills, and the 8 names in the list beside the map are not linked to pins as far as the capture shows (unverified). The map answers 'is there one near me' only roughly, and the list leaves out three centres that /classes offers. 'Fun' is a taste judgement: on-brand, yes.

claims.evidence: Outside conversion, customer and story criteria; left to the visual and motion jurors. The digest records only that 58 endless loops (none with text) and 18 shadowed boxes exist; no stills show which circular parts move.

ref-0009.subpages: classes: the real money page; stock per class, filters and a waitlist are excellent, but no price ('Prorated at Checkout'), 31 tiny tap targets and a 12444px phone page. method: gives the 'Progression' substance (10 numbered steps; the founders named as authors) and clear level ladders with entry criteria, so a parent can self-place; strong for story, but no price or schedule on it. coaches: 40+ named staff with titles prove scale, but they are names and photos only, with no credentials beyond the word 'certified' in the intro. private: transparent price grid with group and volume discounts and a useful FAQ, which breaks at checkout (ActiveNet plus a receipt upload per lesson); 'Dates Available: April to October' plus 'Registration is open' on a 2 Nov capture reads as stale or contradictory. about: supplies the missing trust (city partnership, First Nations programmes, 2000+ students a year, started with 100 at Kerrisdale), none of which reaches the home hero.
problems: No price anchor on the home page, and group-class prices are not shown anywhere on the site; the private-lesson checkout splits across ActiveNet plus a per-lesson receipt upload, a 4-step chain that loses buyers.

The hero's trust is an unbacked superlative ('VANCOUVER'S BEST') and an unsourced '10,000 students', while the checkable proof (City of Vancouver / Park Board partnership, since 2012, 2000+ students a year, named coaches) is buried on the About page or at the bottom of the home page.

Phone friction where the money is: testimonials hidden in a carousel (12 texts never seen during a scroll, hidden under reduced motion), 31 tap targets under 24px on /classes, the home location list does not match the class filter, and private dates look out of season.
keep: Two paying routes split in the header and hero and kept visible (Group vs Private): it routes the two buyer types on the first tap.

Class cards with real stock ('1 spot left'), day, time, venue and number of sessions, plus filters by age, level, day and location: they answer 'is there one for us, when, near me' and create honest urgency.
A 'notify me when registration opens' form tied to lesson and location preferences: it captures demand when the stock is full or the term is closed, instead of ending in a dead end.
Private price grid (group size x number of lessons, per person, 'BEST VALUE' column): a volume discount people can read at a glance, which pulls them toward bigger bundles.
Level ladders with entry criteria ('Can rally 10 in a row...'): parents and adults can place themselves without a call.
A method slogan repeated as a text-on-path band before the method section: brand motion that carries the main message instead of decoration.
ref-0009.veto: None. 'Vancouver's best' is puffery rather than a checkable fact, and 'over 10,000 students' is unsourced but consistent with the About page (since 2012, 2000+ students a year now; inference). Neither is a promise the business cannot keep. Flag: back the hero with the checkable facts, or drop the superlative.
